articles.title: Your first show
articles.summary: Get a DJ account, test your stream and go live.
articles.keywords: first beginner handbook onboarding butt mixxx live broadcast

blocks.text: Ask in #tilderadio about doing a show. An administrator will create your DJ streaming account and enable website access.

items.label: Sign in to the DJ booth

blocks.text: Keep your DJ password private.
Sign in to the DJ booth to edit your profile, book airtime, prepare a playlist and manage broadcasts. The page guide explains which control to use.
Use these settings for the main station with your own DJ username and password. Ask an administrator for connection details if you use another station.
Use port 8015 for the test station. Ask an administrator to confirm your test account access. Check the sound, levels and metadata using headphones or another device.

items: Book a slot in your assigned station schedule. Saving a playlist does not book airtime.
Prepare a title and song list if you want one. Link your IRC account to use the DJ bot commands.
Connect your broadcaster at your slot. Check that the station and Live / IRC show you as the live DJ.
For a prepared playlist, use Start next song or !track next as each song starts. Otherwise Carrier records the stream metadata.
Song announcements start off. Enable them for this show if you want them.
Disconnect when finished, then check your listing in Sets / broadcasts.

blocks.text: Select the right microphone or application output in your broadcaster and check it on the test station.
Ask in #tilderadio. Include your software, operating system and the error message. Leave out passwords and linking codes.

articles.title: Website pages
articles.summary: Where to edit your profile, schedule, playlist or broadcast listing.
articles.keywords: navigation schedule plan listing booth profile difference timezone UTC

rows: Change my bio or recurring show name
Your public DJ page and recurring show defaults
Plan one episode and its song order
A preparation for one broadcast window
Advance songs or manage tonight’s interaction
Fix titles, times or a past track list
The recording attached to a published listing
Activate another DJ or assign a station

blocks.text: Your profile holds recurring show details. A schedule entry books airtime. A preparation holds a title and playlist for one broadcast. Sets / broadcasts holds the archive listing. Each is saved separately.
Schedule times use the station timezone shown in the editor. Preparations and broadcast listings use UTC. Your profile timezone selects weekday show formats.

DJs edit their own assigned profiles, schedules, preparations and listings. The live DJ controls the current broadcast; administrators can manage other DJs. Carrier and recording controls appear when those services are enabled.

articles.title: Website login
articles.summary: Sign in with your DJ streaming username and password.
articles.keywords: login password authenticate azuracast credentials disabled assignment streamer id station

items: Open the DJ booth and enter your DJ streaming username and password.
If website access is disabled, ask an administrator to enable it.
If your profile or station is missing, ask an administrator to check your assignments.

blocks.text: Website access must be enabled for your DJ account. An administrator links it to your public profile and the station accounts you can edit. Changing your display name does not change those assignments.

items: Password not accepted: use your DJ streaming credentials, not an AzuraCast admin login.
Website access disabled: contact an administrator.
Too many attempts: wait five minutes.
Form expired: reload the page.
Temporarily unavailable: try again later. The site cannot check your account right now.

blocks.text: Use Sign out when finished on a shared computer.

articles.title: Streaming setup
articles.summary: Connection settings for BUTT, Mixxx and other Icecast broadcasters.
articles.keywords: butt mixxx broadcast port mount 8005 128 mp3 ogg icecast connection SSL

blocks.text: Other stations may use different ports or accounts. Use the details supplied for your station. A listening URL is not a broadcaster connection.

items: Open Settings and add a server.
Choose Icecast and enter the host, port, mount, DJ username and password.
Select your audio input and encoder. 128 kbps MP3 is the handbook’s suggested starting setting.
Test first, then connect to the main station at your slot.

blocks.text: Open Preferences → Live Broadcasting, choose Icecast 2 and enter the station settings. Select your encoder and test the connection. AzuraCast’s software guide includes Ogg Vorbis settings.
Keep broadcaster config files private. Use the station’s TLS settings if supplied; an HTTPS website does not mean the DJ port accepts TLS. Ask an administrator about certificate errors.

articles.title: Test your stream
articles.summary: Check your sound and metadata on the test station before going live.
articles.keywords: test station 8015 8010 sound silent clipping levels

blocks.text: Connect to azuracast.tilderadio.org on DJ port 8015. Confirm that your account can use the test station.

items: Select the microphone, mixer or application audio you will broadcast.
Play a track and test the microphone.
Listen on headphones or another device. Allow for the stream delay.
Check for clipping and balance the microphone against the music.
Change the artist/title metadata and check that it updates.
Disconnect, then select the main station connection for your show.

blocks.text: Keep the station’s delayed playback out of the audio you send back to it.

articles.title: Audio routing
articles.summary: Send the right audio to your broadcaster and avoid feedback.
articles.keywords: linux pipewire pulseaudio pactl pavucontrol microphone feedback loopback null sink mixer

items: Choose the music and microphone sources you need.
Select the input or mixer in your broadcaster.
Route those sources to that input using your desktop audio tools.
Check the result on the test station using headphones or another device.

blocks.text: Keep station playback and desktop notifications out of the broadcast audio.

Use your desktop mixer to select the broadcaster’s recording input. Choose the device or monitor that carries your audio. PipeWire’s pw-link can also list and connect ports; see its command reference below.
This creates a PulseAudio-compatible output. Route your music application into it, then select its monitor in the broadcaster. Use this only if you need a virtual sink.

pactl load-module module-null-sink sink_name=tilderadio_mix sink_properties=device.description=TildeRadio_Mix
pavucontrol

In your mixer, send the music application to TildeRadio_Mix and select Monitor of TildeRadio_Mix in the broadcaster. Mixing a microphone needs an additional route. Keep the returned module ID so you can unload it later.

articles.title: Edit your DJ profile
articles.summary: Change your biography, links, avatar and recurring show details.
articles.keywords: bio biography avatar genres favorites show title timezone formats weekday JSON git

items: Sign in and open My profile.
Update your name, biography, avatar, links and other profile fields.
Update your recurring show title, description, genres and timezone.
Save and check your public DJ page.

blocks.text: If My profile is unavailable, ask an administrator to link your account to a profile.

The formats field accepts JSON. Give each format a lowercase ID and weekdays in days. Title, tagline, description and genres are optional. Carrier uses your show timezone to choose the format. Use a preparation or Live / IRC for one episode’s title.
An unpublished profile is hidden from the DJ directory. Do not include passwords or other private details.
You can also edit the profile JSON files in Git and run the validator. See the file reference below.

articles.title: Book or change airtime
articles.summary: Add, edit or remove a slot in your assigned station schedule.
articles.keywords: schedule airtime slot overlap conflict timeslot timezone overnight recurring days cancel delete

items: Find Your assigned schedules in the DJ booth.
Choose a station.
Reload its schedule and enter the dates, weekdays and start/end times.
Save. Overlapping slots are rejected.

blocks.text: Choose a free slot, or arrange a change with the other DJ and an administrator. If the schedule has changed since you opened it, reload before saving. A rejected save does not book the slot.
Use the station timezone shown in the editor. Check the selected dates and weekdays for a show crossing midnight. Preparations and archive listings use UTC instead.
Open your schedule entry to change its times or remove it. DJs can edit their own assigned entries; admins have wider access. Cancelling a slot leaves past broadcasts in the archive.
Once your slot is booked, you can prepare its title and playlist. Preparations and planned archive listings do not book airtime.

articles.title: Prepare a show
articles.summary: Save an episode title and song list before your broadcast.
articles.keywords: playlist setlist song order copy plan UTC artist title tab spreadsheet immutable reminder upcoming preview

items: Book airtime, then open Prepare a show → Prepare a new show.
Choose the station and expected start/end in UTC. The window can be up to twelve hours.
Enter the episode title and any topic, mood, prompt, note or link.
Enter songs as Artist | Title, one per line. You can also paste two tab-separated spreadsheet columns.
Choose whether to publish a title/topic preview, send an IRC reminder or announce songs.
Save before connecting. Allow time for Carrier to sync.

blocks.text:
Artist One | Song One
Artist Two | Song Two

Carrier looks for one enabled preparation matching your station account and time window. With no match or several matches, it records normal stream metadata. It copies the preparation when the broadcast starts; later edits do not change that copy.

No songs are marked played at first. Use Start next song or !track next when song one begins, then advance as each song starts. Jumping to a number marks only that song. Unplayed songs are kept out of public feeds.

items.label: Advance songs and choose tracking mode

blocks.text: Edit or cancel an unused preparation, or copy it for another show. Once attached to a broadcast, use live controls or the archive editor for changes. Copies need new times and start with song announcements off. Cancelling a preparation leaves the airtime booking in place.
A preview publishes the title/topic; the unplayed playlist stays private. Reminders go to a linked IRC services account when Carrier can deliver them. Both are optional.

articles.title: Live controls
articles.summary: Change show details, advance songs and manage listener requests during your show.
articles.keywords: live IRC requests question queue poll listener goal handoff mood topic prompt

blocks.text: Open Live / IRC after connecting your broadcaster. Carrier must confirm that you are the live DJ for the assigned station. The page shows your title, listeners, current song and tracking mode.

rows: Enable or disable automatic song messages for this show
Episode title, topic, mood, prompt, note and link
Open requests and resolve queued listener items
Set a goal or run a poll
Name the DJ expected to take over
Post a note if Mastodon is enabled

blocks.text: The live DJ and admins can change the broadcast. After connecting, give Carrier time to update and reload the page. If Carrier is offline or cannot confirm your account, live changes are blocked. Profile, schedule and archive editors use their own checks.
Reload and check the song number or queue before trying again. Retrying the same pending action does not advance twice. Selecting the current song leaves its start time unchanged.

articles.title: Link your IRC account
articles.summary: Link your IRC services account to use DJ bot controls.
articles.keywords: link services account tag nickserv sasl nickname network identity code expiry permission verified

items: Open Live / IRC on the website.
Generate a code under Your IRC accounts.
Log in to IRC services on the network where Carrier is connected.
Send !link CODE in a private message to Carrier.
Refresh Live / IRC to check the account link.

blocks.text: /msg carrier !link YOUR_ONE_TIME_CODE

Playlist and song-announcement controls require an identified IRC services account, not just a matching nickname. The link survives nickname changes. Link each network separately. You must still be the live DJ or an admin. Explicit bot account mappings can also grant access.
Codes expire after five minutes and work once. Keep them private; generate a new one if it expires or is exposed. Remove unwanted links on the same page. Admins can revoke other users’ links.

articles.title: Track songs during your show
articles.summary: Use the website or !track to record when a prepared song starts.
articles.keywords: !track !next start next song jump number metadata prepared captured timestamps positions replay

items: With a prepared playlist attached, use Start next song or !track next when the first song starts.
Repeat for each song.
To jump, select a song number or use !track N. Skipped songs remain unplayed.
Use !track to check the position.

blocks.text:
!track
!track next
!track 5
!next shows the next scheduled broadcast. Use !track next to advance a song.
Selecting the current song keeps its start time. Retrying the same website action does not advance twice. To replay a song, select a different number first, then select it again.

Prepared mode publishes the songs you confirm from your list. Metadata mode uses the artist/title sent by the stream. Carrier keeps the raw metadata in both modes. An empty preparation uses metadata mode.
Switching to metadata ends the current prepared song’s timing. When switching back, select or advance a song to start timing it. Selecting the same mode again changes nothing.
Check that one preparation matches your station account and time window. You can keep broadcasting with metadata capture and fix the track list in Sets / broadcasts later.

items.label: Fix a track list after the show

articles.title: Song announcements
articles.summary: Enable or disable automatic IRC song messages for a show.
articles.keywords: !songs announce announcements automatic quiet silent bot song notification off default on

blocks.text: Song announcements start off unless enabled in the show’s preparation. Use Enable song announcements or Disable song announcements in Live / IRC, or use !songs from your linked IRC account.

!songs on
!songs off
!songs status

The setting lasts for this broadcast and survives bot restarts. It resets for the next show. Copies of preparations start with it off. Website and IRC controls change the same setting; reload the page after using IRC.

Metadata mode announces a new artist/title. Prepared mode announces the song you start. Enabling announcements mid-song waits for the next change. Repeated polls, song selections and retried actions do not send duplicate messages.

Carrier keeps recording songs and updating the archive when announcements are off. !np and !track still work. Other station messages are separate. Invited channels also choose whether to receive announcements.

articles.title: Requests, questions and polls
articles.summary: Manage listener queues, goals and polls from Live / IRC or IRC.
articles.keywords: requests questions !requests !qanswer !qskip !played !reject !goal !poll queue dedicate listener

blocks.text: Requests start closed. Open them in Live / IRC or with !requests on. Mark queued items played or rejected as you handle them. This updates the queue; it does not play audio or advance your playlist.

!requests on
!requests list
!played 3
!reject 4
!requests off
Listeners can ask through IRC or the live activity page. View, answer or skip questions from the queue. Unanswered questions and queued requests stay private.

!questions
!qanswer 2
!qskip 3
Answering through Carrier announces the question. Give your answer on the stream.
Set a listener-count goal and optional message, or clear the goal. Carrier reports when it is reached.

!goal 10 tonight we try the mystery record
!goal clear
Enter a question and at least two options separated by |. Listeners vote with !vote N or on the website. They can change their vote until the poll closes.

!poll start next mood? | ambient | loud | strange
!poll
!poll stop

articles.title: End a show or hand off
articles.summary: Arrange the changeover, disconnect and check your archive listing.
articles.keywords: handoff relay next DJ autodj end stop stream disconnect final set

blocks.text: Set the next DJ in Live / IRC or use !handoff nextdj before disconnecting. Carrier can recognize the handoff after a short AutoDJ gap. The command does not book airtime or connect the other DJ.
!handoff nextdj

items: Agree timing with the next DJ if someone is following.
Disconnect your broadcaster.
Wait for Carrier to close and export the set, then open Sets / broadcasts.
Check the title and tracks, and review a recording if available.

articles.title: Edit broadcast listings
articles.summary: Fix a title or track list, add a missing set, or hide a listing.
articles.keywords: set broadcast session CRUD add edit remove delete hide restore missing title track metadata JSON archive

items: Open Sets / broadcasts.
Select the set and edit its title, show details, DJ name, UTC times or recording link.
Save and check it in the public archive.

blocks.text: The track list uses JSON. Leave Replace the track list unchecked to keep using Carrier’s captured updates. Check it to publish your edited list instead.
Keep the existing played_at and duration fields if you want to retain the timing. An empty replacement list removes the published tracks.

Choose Add a set and enter its profile, UTC times, status and details. DJs add sets for their assigned profile; admins can choose another owner. A planned listing does not book airtime or prepare a playlist.
Deleting hides the listing from the website and API. Captured data and audio remain stored. An admin can restore it. DJ accounts and schedule entries are managed separately.
Reload and review the latest listing before saving. The editor checks for newer edits and capture updates.

articles.title: Recordings and podcasts
articles.summary: Approve available recordings or add a hosted recording to a broadcast.
articles.keywords: recording audio download approve reject podcast rss feed discovery private published mp3

blocks.text: Open Recordings. If recording discovery is enabled, available audio for a completed broadcast may appear for its owner. Review it, then approve or reject it.

Approval attaches the recording to the listing. It becomes public when the listing is published and visible, and the approved recording is valid. The station can disable discovery or downloads. Some shows may have no recording.
Enter the recording URL in your broadcast listing. Check that you have permission to publish it and that the title and times are correct.
Completed, published episodes with suitable recording details appear in the podcast feed. Hidden listings and unapproved private recordings are excluded.

articles.title: Carrier guide
articles.summary: Station commands, listener features and DJ controls.
articles.keywords: carrier bot guide commands IRC stream set track live website

blocks.text: Carrier reads the live station state from AzuraCast, uses your profile and prepared show details, and records sets for the archive. Start and stop your stream in your broadcaster.

!np
!next
!listeners
!dj
!schedule
!next shows the next scheduled DJ. Use !track next for the next prepared song.
Use !tunein [tilde] to join the live show’s roll call and !tuneout to leave it. !couch and !tildes show who is listening.
Give props, ask a question, react, request a song when requests are open, or vote in a poll. Some features are also on the live activity page.
Use Live / IRC for song starts, announcements, show details, listener queues, goals and polls. Link your IRC account to use DJ bot commands.
Check the captured set on the website. Edit missing titles or tracks and approve a recording if available.
When configured, the live DJ can post one note per set. Automatic station posts have separate settings.
Use !handoff nextdj to name the DJ following you. They still need a booking and a connected broadcaster.
Carrier has challenges, bingo, tilde battles, The Button and temporary show commands.
!setcmd name response adds a command for this set. !delcmd name removes it. Built-in commands cannot be replaced.

!last
!set 184
!djstats deepend
!stationstats
!records
!achievements
Invite Carrier on a network where it is connected. Each invited channel chooses whether to receive station announcements.
Book a slot, prepare a show if wanted, connect, track songs during the broadcast, then disconnect and check the archive.

articles.title: Listening and IRC
articles.summary: Listen to the station and use requests, questions, reactions and polls.
articles.keywords: listen couch tunein props ask react request dedicate vote public live interaction

blocks.text: Use the website player or a URL from !listen. The schedule lists airtime, DJs lists profiles, and the archive lists past shows. Upcoming shows can have published episode previews.

rows: Join or leave the live show’s voluntary couch roll call
See the room and represented communities
Queue a question for the DJ
React or inspect the room’s reaction summary
Request a song when the DJ has requests open
Submit a dedication when requests are open
See an open poll or vote for an option

blocks.text: Use the live activity page for questions, open requests, reactions and polls while Carrier is online. No DJ login is needed. Queued questions and requests are visible to the DJ.
Commands and submissions have cooldowns. Wait if Carrier asks you to. The DJ can close requests or turn off song announcements.

articles.title: Carrier in other channels
articles.summary: Invite the bot and choose whether your channel receives station announcements.
articles.keywords: invite channel announce subscription operator owner part carrier announcements on off

blocks.text: Invite Carrier on a connected network if invites are enabled. Use its nickname on that network. Invited channels are remembered across restarts.
/invite carrier #yourchannel

rows: Subscribe this invited channel to station announcements
Keep commands available while disabling station announcements
Remove Carrier and forget the invited channel

blocks.text: The inviter, a channel operator or a bot admin can change these settings when authorized by the bot configuration.

!carrier announce controls the channel’s station announcements. !songs controls song messages for the live show. Both must be enabled for that channel to receive automatic song messages. Commands such as !np still reply in the channel.

articles.title: Games and show commands
articles.summary: Challenges, bingo, tilde battles and commands for one set.
articles.keywords: challenge answer random results bingo battle button temporary setcmd delcmd fun

blocks.text:
!challenge name a song you secretly love
!answer your answer
!challenge results
!challenge random
!challenge stop
The DJ starts or stops a challenge. Listeners submit answers; results and random draws are available during the challenge.
!bingo sends you a random 3×3 card privately. Some events mark squares automatically. The live DJ can mark other events.

!bingo
!bingo marks
Use !bingo marks to list keys. The DJ uses !bingo mark KEY to mark an event.

!battle start tilde.club | ctrl-c.club
!battle
!battle stop
Join a community with !tunein your.tilde. The live DJ starts and stops battles.
Use !button when enabled. It has a cooldown. !fun lists other commands.

!setcmd lore https://example.com/show-lore
!lore
!delcmd lore
The live DJ can add a response command for the current set. It expires when the set ends. Built-in command names are reserved.

articles.title: Mastodon notes
articles.summary: Post one DJ note per set when Mastodon is enabled.
articles.keywords: mastodon federation transmission post note announcement social cooldown

blocks.text: During your show, enter a Mastodon note in Live / IRC or use !show mastodon followed by the text. Posting must be enabled by the station.
!show mastodon tonight is mostly weird synths
The bot’s station settings control automatic posts and cooldowns. Song announcements affect IRC only. Check whether a failed post was sent before retrying.

articles.title: Manage DJ access
articles.summary: Enable website accounts, link profiles and assign stations.
articles.keywords: admin administrator activation DJ accounts streamer id username picker station mapping roles profile disabled delete restore

items: Open Administration → DJs and choose the account editor.
Select the login station and DJ username from the AzuraCast directory.
Enable website login, choose a role and link the DJ’s profile.
For each station assignment, select that station’s DJ username.
Save. The site checks the selected account with AzuraCast.

blocks.text: Accounts are identified by a station/streamer pair. The same DJ can have different accounts in different stations. Select usernames from the directory; manual IDs are available if lookup fails.
Admins can manage other DJs, profiles, schedules and listings. Protected admins are set in the private server configuration and cannot be removed through the account form.

Disable a website account to block login and editing. Deleting removes website access and assignments but leaves the AzuraCast account, public profile and captured broadcasts. Restore deleted website accounts from the DJ list.
Activity lists website changes. Carrier integration shows sync status and recent actions.

articles.title: Carrier status
articles.summary: Check synchronization, live account matching and recording availability.
articles.keywords: health offline carrier sync verification broadcasts recordings discovery schedule API directory timeout fail closed

blocks.text: Open Administration → Carrier integration. Check sync status, account assignments and the age of radio data. Live changes sync first; periodic sync keeps assignments current.

Live changes need current permissions and a confirmed live DJ account. An offline bot, stale sync or failed account check blocks them. Profile, schedule and broadcast editors remain available when their own checks pass.

Discovery needs a completed broadcast, a confirmed owner and an available AzuraCast recording. The admin enables discovery and downloads. The DJ approves publication. A missing recording does not remove the broadcast or tracks.
The repository docs cover installation, keys, socket permissions, updates and rollback.

articles.title: Troubleshooting
articles.summary: Login, streaming, scheduling, playlist and recording problems.
articles.keywords: error help troubleshoot failure offline unavailable 403 conflict stale expired no sound cannot connect

blocks.text: Ask an admin to check account activation, profile link and station assignments. For a password error, check your DJ streaming credentials.

Check the host, DJ port, mount, Icecast mode and account details. Check routing and levels on the test station. Include the broadcaster’s error message when asking for help, but leave out the password.

Reload the schedule. Check the station timezone, look for overlaps and try an available slot. A stale entry or failed upstream check can also block a save. Confirm it saved before treating the slot as booked.

Check that your broadcaster is on the assigned station and the site shows you live. Give Carrier time to update, then reload Live / IRC. Ask an admin to check the station/streamer assignment and Carrier status. A matching display name is not enough.
Check the station, owner, enabled state and UTC window. One unused preparation must match. If none or several match, Carrier captures normal metadata. You can fix the archive later.
Log in to IRC services and link your account on that network. Check that your website assignment matches the live station account.

In prepared mode, start each song with !track or the website control. In metadata mode, send a changed artist/title. Enabling announcements mid-song waits for the next change. Invited channels must also have announcements enabled.
The show may still be live, recording may be disabled, or discovery may not have found a recording for it. Ask an admin to check. You can also add a permitted hosted recording URL to the listing.
Reload and check the result before sending another action. A new Next action advances again. Reload a stale form rather than forcing it to submit.

items: Software and operating system.
Page or command used.
Error message and time.
DJ username, station and set number, if relevant.
Leave out passwords, keys and linking codes.

articles.title: Contribute to the station
articles.summary: Submit an ID, jingle, event idea or guest show.
articles.keywords: community contribute station ID jingle audio license event takeover relay submissions git

blocks.text: Bring your ID or jingle to #tilderadio with its title, creator credit and reuse permission. See the contribution page for formats and length.
Include the idea, length, possible dates and times, participants and any handoffs. Agree the plan with the station before publishing it.
You can submit audio and metadata through the repository, or bring the file to IRC and ask for help submitting it.

articles.title: Profile JSON files
articles.summary: Edit a DJ profile through Git instead of the website editor.
articles.keywords: git JSON profile sample validation formats file slug

blocks.text:
git clone https://github.com/TildeRadio/site.git
cd site
cp data/djs/example.json.sample data/djs/your-nick.json
$EDITOR data/djs/your-nick.json
php bin/validate-djs.php
Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens for the profile filename. Run the validator before submitting your profile and avatar changes. Do not add credentials.
The README lists biography, avatar, links, show, timezone, formats and favorites fields. You can also use My profile on the website.

articles.title: Public API and feeds
articles.summary: Station JSON, episode previews and podcast feeds.
articles.keywords: API JSON endpoint podcast rss terminal curl now history planned schedule episodes djs developer

rows: Podcast feed for eligible recorded episodes

blocks.text: These feeds need no API key. Private playlists, listener queues and unpublished recordings are excluded. Archive edits and hidden listings affect what the feeds publish. Editing requires the separate authenticated controls.

articles.summary: Command syntax and who can use each control.
articles.keywords: command reference help all bot aliases syntax

blocks.text: Examples use !. Your network may use another prefix. Some commands need a live set, an identified IRC services account or admin access. Link your account for playlist and song controls. Older DJ grants still work for the controls they cover. Replies may be private and commands have cooldowns.
